questions.explain: The Quad (India, US, Japan, Australia) launched this to keep an eye on 'dark ships'—vessels that turn off their location transponders to smuggle goods or fish illegally. It's basically high-tech ocean monitoring.

questions.q: In November 2025, which ministry launched the 'Nipun Bharat 2.0' roadmap focusing on foundational literacy?
options: Ministry of Women and Child Development
questions.explain: The Ministry of Education is pushing hard to ensure that every child attains foundational literacy and numeracy by grade 3. The '2.0' version brings in more digital tools and better assessment methods.

questions.q: Which country recently became the first to legally ban the use of lab-grown meat in school cafeterias to protect its traditional dairy and farming industry?
questions.explain: Italy is very protective of its culinary heritage. They’ve passed this law to shield local farmers from what they call 'synthetic' food alternatives. It's a massive cultural debate over there!

questions.q: The 'Green Hydrogen Corridor' project in India is aimed at decarbonizing which specific sector?
questions.explain: Heavy-duty trucking is one of the hardest parts of the economy to green-up because batteries just don't have the range yet. Green hydrogen is our best bet for those long-haul trucks.

questions.q: Who was awarded the 2025 Booker Prize for Fiction, announced mid-November?
questions.explain: Samantha Harvey took it home this year for her novel 'Orbital'. It’s a fascinating, slim book about astronauts watching the Earth, which feels incredibly relevant right now.

questions.q: The Supreme Court of India recently issued a new directive regarding 'Right to be Forgotten'. Under which fundamental right does this largely fall?
questions.explain: The Right to Privacy is part of the Right to Life under Article 21. The Court is essentially saying that if you've served your time or a matter is resolved, you have the right to ask for your sensitive data to be taken offline.
